E035-01.notes: Singular possessive: 'more than a week's wait' (article 'a' requires singular). A lacks apostrophe; B is plural possessive conflicting with 'a'; D is nonstandard. Fact check: ~3+ weeks by stagecoach vs ~10 days saves more than a week; consistent.

E035-02.notes: Subject is 'Each rider'; 'along with the mail he carried' is a parenthetical that does not make the subject plural. 'was expected' matches singular subject and past-tense narration. C/A plural; D plural and wrong tense.

E035-03.notes: 'he swapped ... and rode on' is a compound predicate with one subject; no comma before 'and'. B semicolon and C colon both require an independent clause after; 'and rode on' is not one.

E035-04.notes: Only C conveys speed with a specific, hedged figure ('as little as two minutes, by some accounts'), consistent with commonly cited accounts. A, B, D are vague; D even implies slowness. Also fits 'so' logic after horses waiting saddled.

E035-05.notes: Parallelism with 'both brave and ___' requires an adjective: 'both brave and light'. C (infinitive) and D (clause) break parallelism; A is wordy and nonparallel.

E035-06.notes: Idiom: 'capable of'. A, B, C are unidiomatic.

E035-07.notes: Detail follows 'capable of remarkable feats' and illustrates speed. B wrong (next sentence pivots to money); C contradicts passage (telegraph gap still existed); D unsupported. Fact check: Lincoln's March 4, 1861 address carried Fort Kearny, NE to Fort Churchill, NV (telegraph termini) in about 7 days 17 hours; 'under eight days' accurate.

E035-08.notes: Paragraph shifts from mochila/speed feats to finances at 'Despite such feats, the company was losing money.' A is already the paragraph's first sentence (not a valid split point); B and C continue the speed/feats topic.

E035-09.notes: Past-tense narration ('completed', 'would close') requires 'announced'. Fact check: telegraph completed Oct 24, 1861; Pony Express closure announced Oct 26, 1861 (two days later) - accurate.

flags: minor: the passage never gives the company's formal name (Central Overland California and Pike's Peak Express Company), so 'became known by a simpler name' in paragraph 1 has no stated referent for comparison; consider naming it.
E035-10.notes: Only A addresses both short life (~18 months, April 1860 to Oct 1861 - accurate) and why it is remembered. B shifts focus to the telegraph company; C (pay) and D (eight states) are true-ish trivia that do not explain lasting memory.
